verses.text: Watch your step when you go to God's house. It's better to come close and listen than to offer the sacrifice fools bring. They don't even know they're doing wrong.
Don't let words fly out of your mouth or rush to say whatever's on your heart before God. God's in heaven and you're on earth, so keep your words few.
Many worries will fill your sleep with dreams, and a fool fills the air with words.
When you make God a vow, don't put off keeping it. Fools don't please him. Do what you promised.
It's better to skip the vow than make one and fail to keep it.
Don't let your mouth talk you into sin. Don't tell the messenger, “I made a mistake.” Why make God angry at what you say and have him wreck what your hands built?
Piles of dreams can all slip away like a breath, and so can piles of words. Stand in awe of God.
If you see poor people oppressed and justice and fairness torn away in some district, don't be shocked. One official has a higher official watching them, and others sit above them too.
What the land produces is for everybody. Even the king gets his share from the fields.
Love money and you'll never have enough money. Love having more and you'll never be satisfied with what comes in. That too slips away like a breath.
The more goods there are, the more people show up to eat them. What does the owner get besides a chance to look at it all?
A worker sleeps sweetly after eating a little or a lot. Rich people have so much they can't sleep.
I've seen something awful under the sun. Someone holds on to their wealth, and it ends up hurting them.
Then a stroke of bad luck wipes the money out. If they've had a son, there's nothing left to put in his hand.
They came out of their mother's womb naked, and they'll leave the same way. They won't carry off a single thing they worked for.
That's another terrible wrong. People leave exactly as they came. What does anybody gain from working for the wind?
They spend their days eating in the dark, full of frustration, sickness, and anger.
Here's what I've seen is good and right. Eat, drink, and take some joy in the work you do under the sun in the days God gives you. That's your share.
When God gives someone riches and possessions and lets them enjoy those things, take their share, and find joy in their work, that's God's gift.
They won't spend much time dwelling on how many days they've got, because God keeps their heart busy with joy.
